title: Extend Open-Source Yoroi wallet to support seamless mobile Cardano dApp integration

ms.promise: Open-source repository with the completed wallet integration code for one operating system (either Android or IOS). The next milestone will focus on the 2nd operating system.
ms.criteria: An app running on the same mobile device as the Yoroi can interact with the Yoroi wallet to request the user to sign a transaction, after user confirms, the transaction is signed and submitted to the blockchain.
ms.report:
This milestone has achieved an iOS app running on the same mobile device as the Yoroi Wallet and seamlessly collaborating with the Yoroi Wallet to request the user to sign a transaction to interact with a smart contract. After going through the normal transaction signing process and user confirmation, the transaction is signed and submitted to the blockchain. It supports both sending transaction to a contract and redeeming from a contract.

The video showing a savings demo iOS app interacting with smart contract using Yoroi Wallet:
https://youtu.be/AJpkn94gqc4

ms.report:
This Proof of Achievement covers the final milestone, "Examples and Documentation". It completes the project: milestones 1 and 2 delivered the mobile signing integration for iOS and Android respectively, and this milestone delivers the documentation, code examples, close-out report and close-out video that make that work usable by other developers.
All materials are published under Apache-2.0 in the public repository below, on the feature/contract-spend branch.

A. Output: Code examples showing how to use the integration, in a public GitHub repository.
Acceptance criteria: Code examples are publicly available.
Evidence: https://github.com/bricktowers/yoroi/tree/feature/contract-spend/examples
The repository contains the example mobile application used to record the milestone 1 and milestone 2 demonstrations, with build and run instructions, together with integration recipes covering each supported use case: requesting an ADA payment, requesting an ADA payment with a link, requesting a contract spend, and launching a dApp in the wallet browser. Each recipe shows the code that constructs the link and the wallet screen it opens. Shell scripts for issuing deep links to a booted iOS simulator or Android emulator are included so the flow can be exercised without a physical device.
Recipes: https://github.com/bricktowers/yoroi/tree/feature/contract-spend/docs/mobile-dapp-integration/recipes

B. Output: Documentation on how to integrate mobile dApps with Yoroi, in a public GitHub repository.
Acceptance criteria: Documentation is publicly available.
Evidence: https://github.com/bricktowers/yoroi/tree/feature/contract-spend/docs/mobile-dapp-integration
The documentation covers the integration model, a quick start, the complete link reference for the yoroi:// and https://yoroi-wallet.com/w1 schemes, a full parameter reference for the transfer/request/contract-spend use case, the return path to the calling dApp via redirectTo including Universal Link and App Link configuration,
